title: California's 23rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for California's 23rd Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Jay Obernolte against Democratic challenger Tessa Lynn Hodge, following California's top-two primary on June 2, 2026. The district covers parts of San Bernardino, Riverside, Kern, and Los Angeles counties, encompassing the High Desert and Mojave Desert regions. Obernolte, a video game developer and former mayor of Big Bear Lake who has held the seat since 2021, is seeking a fourth term. Hodge, a licensed clinical social worker and lifelong district resident, is making her first run for public office. The race presents voters with a choice between Obernolte's conservative record focused on fiscal restraint and border security and Hodge's progressive platform emphasizing healthcare access, education funding, and economic opportunity for rural communities.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rated the district as 'Solidly Republican' before the primary.

candidates.name: Jay Obernolte
candidates.summary: Jay Obernolte is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 23rd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. He is a video game developer and business owner who founded FarSight Studios, and previously served in the California State Assembly and as Mayor of Big Bear Lake. In Congress, he serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs the Subcommittee on Research and Technology, and is the only sitting member of Congress with a graduate-level degree in artificial intelligence.

candidates.name: Tessa Lynn Hodge
candidates.summary: Tessa Lynn Hodge is a licensed clinical social worker and first-time candidate running for Congress in California's 23rd District. A lifelong resident of the High Desert, she earned bachelor's and master's degrees in social work from California State University, San Bernardino, and has nearly a decade of experience working with vulnerable populations including foster children and students. Her campaign focuses on healthcare access, education funding, economic development, and what she describes as a need for 'everyday people' in Congress.
